nc_06_three_bears.blurb: Three Bears is a small gully-side wall within Pilot Mountain State Park, on the Piedmont's quartzite. Most of its 15 lines are set up as top-ropes, with a few bolted lines and a single trad route. The grades cover a wide range: several easy 5.5 to 5.8 climbs suit newcomers, one 5.9 sits in the middle, and a solid block of 5.10 and 5.11 lines gives experienced climbers something to chew on. The walk down a stone trail through the woods to the gully is short. Expect an outdoor-gym atmosphere and plenty of company on weekends, and heat in summer.

nc_sunken_treasure.blurb: Sunken Treasure is a small, quiet cliff beside US-221 below the Blue Ridge Parkway, close to Blowing Rock and Grandfather Mountain. It is split into a lower and an upper section, joined by a short gully, and the walls are broken by little roofs. Of its 15 routes, most are trad and three are sport. Grades are centred on 5.10, with a few easier lines around 5.6 to 5.8 and a couple of 5.11s and one 5.12 above them. The walk from the car takes only a few minutes, the lines are short, and the crag is rarely crowded, though traffic noise carries.

nc_trailside_boulder_2.blurb: Trailside Boulder is a single large block in the Trailside Area of the West Side Boulders at Rumbling Bald, near Lake Lure. It holds 15 problems, a friendly spread for a mixed group: about six at V0 or easier and V1, then a few in the V2 to V4 range, topped by five problems at V5. The western face has several V0 lines up a slab and a chimney, plus a crack and a long traverse for those wanting more. It is a good stop for warming up or for climbers new to the grades.

nc_zen_canyon.blurb: Zen Canyon is a trad-only wall tucked into the Gold Coast section of the Linville Gorge, on the gorge's west side. The 15 routes include a few multi-pitch lines alongside single pitches, with one easy 5.5, three 5.9s, and then a heavy dose of 5.10 and 5.11 climbing. A standout feature is an orange face nicknamed the billboard, where many variations are possible. Getting in takes some care: you walk down to the Rock Jock Trail, follow a shared side trail to an overlook, then either rappel in or scramble down a gully. It suits confident trad parties wanting a quiet, adventurous day.
